For \(x<0\), let \(u=-x>0\). Then
\[
f(-x)=f(u)=2u-u^2=-2x-x^2.
\]
Since \(f\) is odd,
\[
f(x)=-f(-x)=x^2+2x.
\]

To minimize \(b\), consider \(b<0\). Then \(a<b<0\), and \([1/b,1/a]\) is a negative interval, so \([a,b]\subset[-2,0]\). If \(b<-1\), then \(a<b<-1\), and on \([-2,-1]\), \(f(x)=x^2+2x\) is decreasing. Thus
\[
[f(b),f(a)]=\left[\frac1b,\frac1a\right],
\]
so \(f(a)=\frac1a\) and \(f(b)=\frac1b\). For \(x<0\),
\[
x^2+2x=\frac1x \implies x^3+2x^2-1=0=(x+1)(x^2+x-1).
\]
The negative roots are
\[
x=-1,\quad x=\frac{-1-\sqrt5}{2}.
\]
There is only one root less than \(-1\), so no \(b<-1\) is possible.

For \(b=-1\), take
\[
a=\frac{-1-\sqrt5}{2}.
\]
Then \(f(-1)=-1=\frac1b\) and \(f(a)=\frac1a\). Hence the range on \([a,-1]\) is
\[
\left[-1,\frac1a\right]=\left[\frac1b,\frac1a\right].
\]
Therefore the minimum value of \(b\) is
\[
\boxed{-1}.
\]
